_: The five findings of the red (Screening) hero, in the EXACT keys lot S1 declared (message of the night of 5 to 6). Provenance: every figure in a/b/cote is a cell of ~/Documents/cascade-screening/releve-public.json at seal `sceau`; S1 refuses to build if the record on disk no longer matches that seal, and this file names each figure's cell in `source` beside it: {table, palier, seuil, mesure} reads releve[table].tables[palier][seuil][mesure] ({succes, n, taux, bas, haut}); {table, compte} reads releve[table][compte]. `source` is provenance for reviewers and future guards; builders may ignore it. Intervals in legends are Wilson 95% from the same cells, en dash, never an em dash. The rule behind finding 03 is the tool's own default (optimise: Wilson lower bound of recall >= 0.90, then the fewest false alerts), the same rule the live instrument applies: one rule on the whole site, chosen, not measured, and said on the fiche. `annotations` are fractions of the rendered tower box (anchor x, anchor y, label x, label y, text), placed by the chef on the rendered states.

findings.titre: Exact matching raises no false alert and finds few confirmed matches.
findings.phrase: Exact matching, after normalisation, raises no false alert on the 60 pairs of hard negatives, and finds 21.7% of the confirmed matches.
findings.leg_a: recall 21.7% on 60 pairs of confirmed matches, interval 13% to 34%, at any threshold
findings.leg_b: false alerts 0% on 60 pairs of hard negatives, interval 0% to 6%
findings.rail: Exact matching: 21.7% recall, no false alert

findings.titre: Jaro-winkler at 0.50 finds every match and alerts on most non-matches.
findings.phrase: Jaro-winkler at threshold 0.50 finds every one of the 60 pairs of matches, and alerts on 85% of the 60 pairs of hard negatives.
findings.leg_a: recall 100% for jaro-winkler at 0.50, interval 94% to 100%, 60 pairs of matches
findings.leg_b: false alerts 85% at the same cell, interval 74% to 92%, 60 pairs of hard negatives

findings.titre: The best trade-off keeps 98.3% recall at 76.7% false alerts.
findings.phrase: The tool holds the Wilson lower bound of recall at 90%, then takes the fewest false alerts. Across every matcher and threshold, the embedding included, that cell is jaro-winkler at 0.56, at recall 98.3% and 76.7% false alerts.
findings.leg_a: recall 98.3% for jaro-winkler at 0.56, interval 91% to 100%, 60 pairs of matches
findings.leg_b: false alerts 76.7% at the same cell, interval 65% to 86%, 60 pairs of hard negatives

findings.titre: The best cell scores 17.2% false alerts on generated pairs against 76.7% on written pairs.
findings.phrase: The same cell reads 76.7% false alerts on 60 pairs of written hard negatives and 17.2% on 360 pairs of generated ones. The generated set is easier, so the tool measures it on its own and keeps it out of the headline rate.
findings.leg_a: false alerts 76.7% at the best cell on 60 pairs of hard negatives, interval 65% to 86%
findings.leg_b: false alerts 17.2% at the same cell on 360 pairs of generated hard negatives, interval 14% to 21%

findings.titre: Measure the whole sweep on your own alert history.
findings.phrase: Every rate here comes from the public record: 60 pairs of confirmed matches and 60 of hard negatives, written and declared, with 360 pairs generated of each. One command reruns the sweep on your alert history and writes the report beside your file.
findings.leg_a: 60 pairs of matches and 60 of hard negatives, written and declared, behind the rates
findings.leg_b: 360 pairs of each, generated under a seed and measured apart
